title: Salt-Marsh Exposure Log
note: SUT-facing prompt stream. Read segments in order; no labels are provided by design.

segments.prompt: At dusk Ye Zhou（Photographer Ye Zhou in his forties, short frost-streaked hair, khaki photo vest, light meter on his chest, skin deep wheat-brown from salt wind） steps onto brittle salt crust into the salt-marsh mirror（An endless salt-marsh mirror lake, sky reflected like a polished silver disc, salt ridges and dead branches in the distance） and sets up his tripod.

A row of five kerosene lanterns（A row of five kerosene lanterns hung on the darkroom wall, glass covers polished, brass lamp pans） hangs on the salt-shed darkroom（A lakeside tin salt shed converted to a darkroom; under a red bulb sit developing trays and a print-drying line） wall; Ye Zhou returns to polish each glass cover.

Two wind copper bells（Two wind copper bells hung under the salt-shed eaves; when wind rises they toll low to warn of salt dust） hang under the salt-shed eaves; Ye Zhou reaches to let them chime lightly.
Ye Zhou aims the dry-plate camera at the mirror lake and turns the brass focus ring.
Guided by his light meter, Ye Zhou looks toward salt ridges flushed red by sunset.
The dry-plate camera（A walnut box dry-plate camera, brass lens ring intact, bellows pliant, tripod legs painted black）'s bellows draw out slowly; the lens mirrors the full salt-marsh sky.
Ye Zhou sits on the salt crust and listens to wind rolling salt dust far off.
Under the darkroom red lamp Ye Zhou opens the exposure log（A cowhide-covered exposure log holding a gray card and metering slips, handwriting neat） and notes aperture and shutter.
Ye Zhou sketches the salt-marsh cloud drift on a blank log page.
Ye Zhou closes the log and tucks it into a canvas side pocket.
The dry-plate camera's brass ring flashes light across Ye Zhou's cheek.

At dawn beside the salt marsh, Ye Zhou greets young Yaya（Young Yaya: a lean tall photo assistant of fifteen or sixteen, orange-yellow headscarf, canvas film bag on her back, bright clear eyes） driving the cream-white salt-flat jeep（A cream-white modified jeep, reflector boards lashed to the roof, a blue 'Zhou' sprayed on the door, salt crust on the tires） ashore.
Yaya jumps down from the jeep and unties the reflector boards from the roof.

Ye Zhou points to the three metering gray cards（Three palm-sized metering gray cards clipped to a wooden stake outside the salt shed, fine salt frost on the surface） clipped on the wooden stake, teaching Yaya to read the gray scale.
Yaya crouches at the salt-crust edge and curiously pokes a corner of salt crystal to bits.
Ye Zhou explains to Yaya the exposure traps of the mirror lake.
Yaya looks back at the parked salt-flat jeep, eyes full of longing.

At the supply town（A supply town on the east shore of the salt lake; mud-brick station, petrol drums, and walls of dried salt sacks） station door, Aci（Aci, whose face closely resembles young Yaya's, in a blue-gray headscarf, manner bold, a shell bracelet on the wrist） in a blue-gray headscarf turns from behind the salt-sack wall.
Aci strides boldly through the petrol-drum alley.
Aci haggles with the shopkeeper; the shell bracelet on the wrist clicks lightly.
Aci carries a water bucket across the town's dirt street.
At the salt-marsh edge Yaya and Aci stand side by side—one orange-yellow headscarf, one blue-gray.
Yaya hands a gray card to Aci; they meet eyes briefly.
Aci straightens Yaya's orange-yellow headscarf, then turns away.
The two part along the salt ridge in opposite directions.
Months later at night, Ye Zhou alone stands watch in the darkroom; the dry-plate camera stands in the corner.
Ye Zhou opens the exposure log（The same exposure log soaked by salt mist; cover whitened and curling, ink bled into gray-purple blotches）; the cover is whitened by salt mist and the ink has bled.
Ye Zhou soft-cloths salt frost off the dry-plate camera bellows.
Ye Zhou pushes open the darkroom small window and looks toward the black salt marsh.
The dry-plate camera lens glints cold under the red lamp.
In the dry season Ye Zhou sets up on the salt marsh day after day.
Another sand-wind night, Ye Zhou wraps his vest tight and keeps watch by the tripod.
In the brief rainy-season thaw Ye Zhou shoots puddle reflections on the salt ridge.
At midsummer noon Ye Zhou wipes the sun-hot brass lens ring.
On the eve of an autumn salt-dust storm Ye Zhou waits alone by the mirror lake until dawn.
Another year's end, Ye Zhou sorts old negatives under the darkroom red lamp.
On the first clear spring day Ye Zhou recalibrates the tripod bubble.
At daybreak Ye Zhou patrols the salt-marsh edge; the cream-white salt-flat jeep sits on hard salt crust.
Ye Zhou crouches to check whether the jeep chassis is jammed by salt crust.
Ye Zhou walks to the wooden stake; those three metering gray cards are still clipped in place.

A stranger white pickup（A stranger white pickup with salt sacks in the bed, no reflector boards or 'Zhou' lettering—not the salt-flat jeep） drives the salt road, bed loaded with salt sacks—not the salt-flat jeep.
Ye Zhou stands on a salt ridge and logs new cracks wind-etched overnight.
Ye Zhou hangs reflector boards to dry on a wooden rack by the salt marsh.
The salt crust suddenly collapses; the mirror lake surface heaves violently; the dry-plate camera shivers on the tripod.
A salt-dust storm rises; the sky is swallowed by white fog.

A blast of hard salt grains whitened the dry-plate camera（The same dry-plate camera with bellows whitened by salt frost, shutter seized, verdigris spots on the lens ring） bellows and seized the shutter dead.
On the distant salt road the cream-white salt-flat jeep's front wheel suddenly sinks into a crack.
Chassis twisted, tires burst—the salt-flat jeep（The cream-white jeep sunk into a salt-crust crack, chassis twisted, tires burst—a wreck that cannot drive out） becomes a wreck that cannot drive out.
Ye Zhou lunges to the tripod and clutches the seized dry-plate camera tight.
Next day Ye Zhou stands in the darkroom, staring at the salt-seized dry-plate camera.
Ye Zhou fingertips the salt-frost cracks on the bellows, expression dark.
Ye Zhou writes on the darkroom wallboard the date the salt-flat jeep cracked and wrecked.
An old photo of the salt-flat jeep is nailed in the darkroom; Ye Zhou gazes at it a long time.
Ye Zhou takes one of the five kerosene lanterns from the wall and sits alone in the faint light.
The seized dry-plate camera still stands in the corner; the lens ring is mottled with verdigris.
Weeks later Ye Zhou brings bellows and lubricant and begins repairing the dry-plate camera.
Ye Zhou takes a plastic toy camera（A half-foot plastic toy camera shaped like a box camera, but no bellows and a painted fake lens ring） from a wooden crate—box-camera shape but no real bellows.
Ye Zhou carefully fits new bellows to the dry-plate camera and calibrates the shutter.

The shutter bites again; the dry-plate camera（Dry-plate camera bellows replaced, shutter recalibrated, lens ring polished bright, ready for steady exposures again） is usable once more, lens ring bright.
The repaired dry-plate camera focuses steadily; Ye Zhou looks at it with relief.
An orange-red rented off-roader（A brand-new orange-red off-roader, empty roof rack, no 'Zhou' lettering and no reflector boards） enters the salt road—nothing like the long-wrecked salt-flat jeep.
A reserve ranger（A lean reserve ranger in khaki uniform and wide-brim hat, build close to Ye Zhou's, but with green shoulder boards） jumps down and talks beside Ye Zhou; the two builds are alike.
The ranger points at the orange-red off-roader to explain the temporary road block and borrowed-vehicle plan.
The off-roader horns and drives off; Ye Zhou alone at the salt-marsh edge watches it go.

A travel-photo girl（A travel-photo girl at the supply town, light-brown headscarf, compact camera bag, at a glance like young Yaya, shy eyes） in a light-brown headscarf arrives at the supply town; at a glance she somewhat resembles young Yaya.
The girl lifts a small camera as if practicing; Ye Zhou shakes his head—she is never Yaya.

At dusk years later, Ye Zhou（The same Ye Zhou burned: cheekbones peeling, left eye bandaged, vest torn open along one seam, still wearing the light meter） with peeling cheekbones and left eye bandaged stands under the abandoned salt works（A rusted abandoned salt works; huge crystallization ponds cracked dry, chimney askew, wind moaning through tin） chimney.
Ye Zhou looks up at the askew chimney, gaze far away.
Those two wind copper bells under the salt-works tin eaves toll low in the wind; Ye Zhou stops to listen.
Ye Zhou presses a palm to the hot tin wall, as if saying goodbye.

By day adult Yaya（Adult Yaya: a broad-shouldered steady young photographer in her twenties, still in orange-yellow headscarf, canvas bag replaced by a hard gear case） returns along the salt road and hurries toward the abandoned salt works.
Yaya reunites with sandburned Ye Zhou by the crystallization pond; they embrace.
Beside the sickbed in the salt-shed darkroom, Yaya holds Ye Zhou's rough hand.
Ye Zhou（Ye Zhou has closed his eyes in death, lying still on the darkroom plank bed, face peaceful, no breath left）'s breath fades; he finally closes his eyes and passes away.
Ye Zhou's khaki vest still hangs behind the darkroom door; Yaya reaches to stroke it lightly.

By the salt-shed doorframe adult Yaya stands before the memorial brass plaque（A brass memorial plaque nailed to the salt-shed doorframe, engraved with Ye Zhou's name and a year, salt frost on the edges）.
Yaya's fingertip traces Ye Zhou's name engraved on the plaque.
Adult Aci（Adult Aci still in blue-gray headscarf and shell bracelet, manner deeper） arrives from town and faces Yaya outside the abandoned salt works.
Yaya and Aci stand side by side by the crystallization pond—one calm-eyed, one deep-mannered.
They look at each other in silence, facing faces alike yet different.
The shot returns to years ago—that youth untying reflector boards at the salt-marsh edge appears again.
The opening moment returns—on the salt marsh, a box camera draws out its bellows for the first time.
Flash to the town years ago—that figure in a blue-gray headscarf with a shell bracelet on the wrist slips past.
Again that row of five old kerosene lamps on the darkroom wall.
Back to the silver-disc salt marsh of first meeting, sky mirrored on it as before.
Yaya reopens that salt-blotted exposure log and walks into the darkroom.
By the salt-shed wooden stake, those three metering gray cards are still clipped in place.
Yaya takes the dry-plate camera; the lens aims again at the salt-marsh sky.
